paragraphs.source_en: The master went on at once: “I have heard a story like this: again in a British barracks, a number of regimental officers together invited a noncommissioned officer to dinner. After the meal, a glass bowl filled with clear water was brought in for washing the hands. The noncommissioned officer, not being very familiar with such banquets, lifted the glass bowl to his mouth and drained all the water in one gulp. At this, the regimental commander suddenly declared that he would drink to the noncommissioned officer’s health, and he too drained the water from his finger bowl in one breath. Then the other officers present, not to be outdone, all raised their finger bowls too and drank to the corporal’s health.”

paragraphs.source_en: Meitei, who never liked to remain silent, said, “There is another story of that sort. When Carlyle first had an audience with the Queen, being an eccentric fellow quite unversed in court etiquette, the gentleman suddenly said, ‘May I?’ and plumped himself down in a chair. At that, the many attendants and ladies-in-waiting standing behind the Queen could not help laughing. Or rather, they did not quite laugh; they were desperately trying not to. Then the Queen turned around and made a slight gesture, and those attendants and ladies-in-waiting sat down one after another. paragraphs.source_en: Dokusen took his turn: “A conscious awareness of kindness is not bad in itself, of course; but precisely because one shows kindness on the premise of such self-awareness, it is bound to be laborious. It is rather pitiable. People generally say that as civilization advances, the murderous, combative spirit disappears and relations between individuals become much more peaceful; but that is a great mistake. With self-consciousness this strong, how could things possibly become peaceful? True, at first glance it may look calm and uneventful, but in fact both sides are suffering terribly. It is no different from sumo wrestlers locked together in the center of the ring, gripping each other and standing motionless. To the bystander it appears perfectly tranquil, but are not the wrestlers themselves secretly exerting tremendous force?”
